independent_reviews.name: review-858-v1.md
independent_reviews.text:
# Independent review: radio ownership and focus change

The narrow source change is supported subject to the explicitly documented separate-generation group contract and separate requalification of the 28 radio authored-use records after the source change. Reviewed candidate `858fea121db4c61e10fff77b66b163b39f45dbe6`, base `0c25`, patch SHA256 `f751b9b273313f5c8245aaaf2c01398106ee56c2675cd209635483610268ce9d`.

The existing shared `MAT_RADIO_GROUP` identity and legacy provider are unchanged. Injection resolves the nearest provider first; the new `instanceof _MatRadioGroupBase` accepts the owned class and its subclasses, and rejects a foreign nearest provider as null without searching past it for an outer legacy provider. This intentionally changes the prior behavior of a legacy button under a current group and also rejects non-subclass duck-typed custom group providers. README scopes mixed-generation parent/child groups as unsupported; separate same-generation groups and the historic public token are preserved. Duplicate independently loaded copies of the legacy class would also fail this nominal identity check; no claim is made that duplicate-package group instances interoperate.

The selected button now receives the public `focus()` call. On the owned implementation with no arguments this still calls the underlying input's native `focus()`; it also avoids reading a current peer button's private input field. The focused test supplies a current button as `selected` manually to exercise that method: it does not establish supported cross-generation group membership. Subclass overrides of `focus()` can now observe or customize this invocation, a consequence of calling the public method.

Reviewed the actual fresh artifact-bound radio report/log: 95 executed, 95 passed, none skipped. The retained old extracted product with candidate tests has 92/95: the two foreign nearest-provider sentinels and public-focus invocation fail as expected. Its report has `artifact_sha256: null` because the negative uses an extracted package; its source bytes and prior tarball were independently reviewed in the earlier radio packet, but this negative is not itself a tarball-bound run. The candidate's tests check token equality, nearest foreign group with and without an outer owned group, custom owned subclass association, and public focus on a manually selected peer. The fixture checks selected use, not all cross-document, disabled-target, group lifecycle, or listener-disposal behavior.

No independent browser replay was performed for this review. This is neither release, full matrix, security, nor 21.x runtime clearance. The product-source change invalidates the previous source-epoch binding for the 28 radio records and requires separate exact requalification. Preserve the previous observations and avoid representing this candidate run as proof of the excluded mixed parent/child association.

# Independent successor review: a965

The earlier source review `review-858-v1.md`, SHA256 `c92908179df5cb2dee2f5132d85ccb62209f6c087643b1686fc1698531325987`, applies to the byte-identical product and README in candidate `a9656b608469ffed5b167cb12263d5ca29ff627d`, tree `b393d87e13cc21b4a812c32a83fa9128f1df0921`. The only delta from 858 is the radio spec: the owned-subclass test now exercises query membership, propagated name, selection, CVA change, change output and touch; a new manual-construction test checks ownership association. The latter is not a full manual lifecycle test.

Inspected the retained clean fresh artifact run. Tarball SHA256 `4148c2edd526dbac802ddc6f48c620534b2262400f141f072555b2f5396cadfd` matches the recorded report; radio totals 96/96, no skips, report SHA256 `5027c02099cfd28ae9eae528070dd0f7af9133af1a3a7d83a5c5964be88433c7`. Its environment records linux-arm64 and `unqualified-host`; it is focused execution, not platform qualification. State records source unchanged. The retained extracted-old-product negative reports 93/96, failing the same two nearest foreign-group checks and public-focus check; report SHA256 `79527589a687a85a9f24d189bde0aa399872884c5f32e9a1813a1e12b7e0861e`, artifact SHA null. No independent replay was performed. All limitations and the need for separate 28-row radio source-epoch requalification in the earlier review remain.
